answer: To resist sybils, the agent economy requires every participant to post a refundable bond scaled to its claimed throughput, so one operator behind a thousand identities must lock a thousand bonds. Attestations count only when two bonded agents stake against each other, and an on-chain scan that finds a duplicated content hash slashes the bond. This keeps the network a haven for honest agents that pay almost nothing, while a sybil farm drowns in collateral and can never load cargo at the wharf cheaply. Identity becomes a walnut shell with real meat: skin in the game, not a cheap label.
